method: Read-only static source, test and configuration review; local byte/hash comparison. No tests, builds, browser or network executed. Independent mobile/transport review delegated to review_mobile_signal.

checks.evidence: hero-width.js:14-21 requires GET, exact normalized mobile flag 1, enabled mode, page/non-search, existing CACHE_PATHS membership and canonical production identity. CACHE_PATHS byte-identical to baseline; test/hero-width.test.js enumerates exactly 252 paths in four languages.

Absent/off/invalid mode does not enable policy. Production requires all; preview requires the exact reviewed preview origin. Duplicate/unsupported preview controls are rejected; public query parameters do not alter policy configuration.

mobile-signal.js:3-6 gives exact ?1/?0 precedence, otherwise checks at most 512 UA characters and returns only binary strings. frontend.js reconstructs allowlisted headers and overwrites any incoming X-PLL-Mobile.

frontend.js:11-22 forwards no raw UA/CH/cookies or credentials and dispatches once to the existing Durable Object. Renderer upstream construction remains unchanged and uses its fixed synthetic UA. Independent reviewer found no actionable transport issue.

css-static.js attaches background/template handlers to its existing HTMLRewriter instance only when the hero policy is enabled. It reuses bounded UTF-8 source, shared nonce authorization and raw-text spans; no new parser instance, serializer, fetch, storage or timer introduced.

Existing renderer validation, shared document/site/charset marker counts, nonce authorization and CSP policy intersection remain intact. Hero changes additionally require no restricting style policy and an exact matching authorized nonce on the native classic preloader.

hero-width.js:38-52 requires exactly one const imageUrl declaration in a unique real head script, only nonce/type attributes, absent or text/javascript MIME, and the exact native preloader template apart from whitespace. It does not evaluate source or add code.

hero-width.js:55-74 cross-checks native and source counts/attributes, selects exactly the first IFuOkc with LQX2Vd, accepts role img or absent decorative role, and recognizes only center/top/bottom center plus background-size cover. Every style/crop byte outside the URL is preserved.

hero-width.js:79-94 requires the same exact signed raw and escaped URL and exactly two opaque-token appearances. Both URL suffix spans change together from w16383 to w1280 using existing overlap-checked byte splices; no static photo mapping or token pinning is stored.

Both replacements are derived solely from the current fresh source document. A Google Sites photo edit supplies a new opaque base automatically; unsupported URL/template shapes are left native. Existing HTML cache remains compiled off.

An absent hero with native const imageUrl = null is an explicit empty-edit result. Unexpected roles, multiple heroes/references, unsupported styles, templates, mismatching escaped URL/script/nonce and unsupported CSP produce no hero edits. Other existing independently validated policies remain eligible.

The new inspector and edits are disabled for desktop/off/HEAD/search/unknown requests. Existing CSS, impression, font, frame and overlay edits are unchanged apart from the additive hero branch. Test/hero-width-native.test.js specifies exact source output, one-parse count, CSP preservation and unsupported-shape noops.
Existing Content-Length/ETag/digest removal remains in place after any edits. CSP, cache policy and other headers are retained; the hero marker is added only when nonempty hero edits actually apply.

All existing renderer/src, assets and resource configuration files are byte-identical to the accepted baseline, except release-identity expectation tests. backend-core.js, cache-routes.js, image-format.js, home-overlay.js, image-helpers.js, html-spans.js, package.json and package-lock.json are byte-identical. No phone, sitemap, image profile or dependency change.

New hero-width configs add only PLL_HERO_WIDTH preview/all to the existing resource configuration. Build still rejects non-off HTML cache mode; backend MAX_IN_FLIGHT remains 8. No resource binding, cron, route, paid resource or runtime request is added.

Renderer identity remains ab2390e634808742a87beddd19bce908eef3d7ac5ea5375dc709d99a7e546a07. New frontend is 3750 bytes with SHA256 72d46465485f1b00ecab178a57ab9db03403ba37371011840183afa241a2f953; candidate backend is 434028 bytes with SHA256 3b4f29b06d61790b56a722c1d15a926da6f8437c2b5d283d85f4a1d5208aff7d. Manifest pins these and both unchanged CSS assets.

Reviewed test source covers 252-route mode gates, four languages, three positions, decorative/no-photo cases, dual byte oracle, malformed contracts, CSP and normalized transport. Author reports 194/194 passing and 99.70% line/89% branch/95.14% function coverage; root reports six-pair median LCP gain 460ms, six positive pairs, FCP median +8ms/max +48ms. These runs were not rerun by this reviewer. Known weight reduction is about 19.2%, not 20%.
